titlePl: Matura PP: Praca — 36 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Matura Basic: Work — 36 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Słownictwo z działu Praca na maturę podstawową: CV, etat, nadgodziny, zwolnienie. Wklejasz listę w LingoSpark i odpalasz lekcję.
blurbEn: Matura basic-level Work vocabulary: CVs, hours, overtime, redundancy. Paste the list into LingoSpark and run the lesson.

items.definitionEn: to formally ask for a job or a place
items.example: She decided to apply for a summer job in a hotel.

items.definitionEn: a written request for a job
items.example: Send your application before the end of the month.

items.definitionEn: a letter sent with a CV to explain why you want the job
items.example: Your covering letter should be no longer than one page.

items.definitionEn: a document listing your education, skills and work history
items.example: Update your CV after every new course or job.

items.definitionEn: a meeting where an employer asks you questions about a job
items.example: He was nervous before the interview on Monday.

items.definitionEn: a person or company that pays people to work
items.example: A good employer trains new staff properly.

items.definitionEn: a person who is paid to work for a company
items.example: Every employee must wear a name badge.

items.definitionEn: without a paid job
items.example: He has been unemployed since the factory closed.

items.definitionEn: a job that is available
items.example: There is a vacancy for a shop assistant in the mall.

items.definitionEn: a period of work in a workplace that operates in turns
items.example: Nurses often work a night shift.

items.definitionEn: extra hours worked after normal work time
items.example: She did overtime last week to finish the report.

items.definitionEn: money paid monthly for professional work
items.example: The starting salary is advertised on the company website.

items.definitionEn: money paid weekly or hourly, often for manual work
items.example: The hourly wage is higher at weekends.

items.definitionEn: extra money paid for good results
items.example: Staff received a Christmas bonus this year.

items.definitionEn: a move to a higher job in the same company
items.example: After two years she got a promotion to team leader.

items.definitionEn: to leave a job by your own decision
items.example: He plans to resign and start his own business.

items.definitionEn: to stop working, usually because of age
items.example: My grandfather will retire next June.

items.definitionEn: a student or graduate working for a short time to gain experience
items.example: The intern helped with social media for six weeks.

items.definitionEn: the last day or time something must be finished
items.example: The deadline for the project is Friday afternoon.

items.definitionEn: a system where you can choose when to start and finish
items.example: Flexible hours help parents collect children from school.

items.definitionEn: a traditional full-time office schedule
items.example: She is tired of a nine-to-five routine and wants freelance work.

items.definitionEn: to travel regularly between home and work
items.example: I commute to Warsaw by train every weekday.

items.definitionEn: a person you work with
items.example: Ask a colleague if you do not understand the task.

items.definitionEn: giving a lot of money for the work
items.example: IT jobs are often well-paid but stressful.

items.definitionEn: needing a lot of effort, skill or time
items.example: Teaching can be rewarding but very demanding.

items.definitionEn: without a job because the company no longer needs that position
items.example: Two hundred workers were made redundant last year.

items.definitionEn: working for yourself, not for an employer
items.example: Many graphic designers are self-employed.

items.definitionEn: to own and manage a company
items.example: They run a business selling handmade jewellery online.

items.definitionEn: the series of jobs you take as you progress
items.example: She is not sure yet which career path to choose.

items.definitionEn: working fewer hours than a full week
items.example: He has a part-time job in a café after school.

items.definitionEn: working the complete normal number of hours
items.example: After university she found a full-time position.

items.definitionEn: lasting only for a limited period
items.example: This is a temporary contract until December.

items.definitionEn: intended to last, not for a short period
items.example: She finally got a permanent post at the library.

items.definitionEn: a statement from a previous employer about your work
items.example: Ask your teacher for a reference if you have never had a job.

items.definitionEn: exams, degrees or certificates that show your skills
items.example: The job requires qualifications in accounting.

items.definitionPl: równowaga między pracą a życiem prywatnym
items.definitionEn: a fair division of time between job and private life
items.example: Long hours can destroy your work-life balance.
